static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; without similar psychological problems before; without previous psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, high cooperation; negative tone, obvious guilt and self-blame, frequently using 'should'-style self-demands; resistant to self-compassion

basic_info.main_problem: Since my beloved cat passed away, I have been struggling with guilt and self-blame. These feelings appeared immediately after losing my cat and have remained very strong and overwhelming.
basic_info.core_demands: Guilt and self-blame have affected my daily functioning and mental health, so I hope to obtain support through counseling.
growth_experiences: After the beloved cat died, strong guilt and self-blame appeared immediately, believing the cause was one's own failure as a pet owner; when thinking about the late beloved cat or interacting with other pets, emotions are strongly triggered; trying to distract with reading and playing with Poppa's train models, but the guilt persists.
Living with Poppa, able to discuss some difficulties with him, but holding back for fear of adding to his burden.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible pet owner
The misfortune that happened is mainly my fault, I need to take full responsibility

special_situations.event: Thinking about the deceased beloved cat
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I were a qualified owner, I should have been able to notice and prevent any signs leading to his death
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly reflecting on details and harshly blaming oneself, hoping to 'prevent repeating it in the future'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I caused his death

special_situations.event: Interacting with other pets or seeing others walk their pets
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure is enough to prove I am a terrible pet owner
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding pet-related contact and comparison, or reducing participation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just a terrible pet owner

special_situations.event: Sees old photos or is reminded of past feelings at home (places where the cat used to stay)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A good owner should always do their best, never making mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Blames herself with 'should', immersed in guilty memories
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have discovered the problem earlier; I should have done better

special_situations.event: Others (such as the counselor or Poppa) giving positive feedback or reminding of uncontrollable factors
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I accept this positive information, it equals making excuses for myself and shirking responsibility
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, persisting in self-blame to maintain a 'responsible' self-image
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Changing thoughts is useless, I should not exonerate myself

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be understood and comforted, and to be confirmed that they have tried their best in caring (becoming a 'good owner')
core_conflict.fear: Fears being blamed for dereliction of duty and seen as a bad person; fears losing control and experiencing loss again
defense_goal: Maintains the feeling of 'I can still control / remedy it' through intense self-blame
Reduces expressing emotions to significant others (such as Poppa) to avoid being seen as 'troublesome'

object_relations.object_representation: A deceased and fragile attachment object unable to respond (the beloved cat)

object_relations.self_representation: One who needs judgment and atonement
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh inner critic / moral judge

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests looking at the event from a broader perspective, distinguishing controllable and uncontrollable factors
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing it as the counselor exonerating oneself, equating to denying one's own fault (transference: worried about being judged as shirking responsibility)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone that validates the sense of responsibility, first acknowledging his love for the pet and his efforts, then gradually distinguishing controllable / uncontrollable; using open-ended questioning guidance rather than direct refutation, reducing vigilance about being 'exonerated'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites practicing self-compassion and recalling positive caregiving moments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views self-compassion as 'making excuses for myself', thus refuses to accept positive information
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keep stable, gentle, and concretizing: first ask them to describe a small and real positive memory, then only name the emotion; avoid preaching, use 'if you were comforting a friend, what would you say' to externalize and turn it back to the self.

manifestations: The death of the beloved cat triggers intense and persistent guilt and self-blame
Repeatedly triggered by life cues (old photos, familiar places, interacting with other pets)
Difficulty accepting uncontrollability, tending to attribute all responsibility to oneself
outcomes: Negating positive memories and caregiving evidence

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly using 'I should / must...' to evaluate oneself
Regarding 'a good owner must prevent all accidents' as an absolute standard
Hard to accept Poppa's positive evaluation of her care

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to do a certain behavior toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others outwardly to do something for them, and instead does it to themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Unwilling to 'trouble' Poppa by expressing emotions and seeking help
Turns the sadness and needs that should be expressed outward into self-punishing self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When strong emotions arise, displacing attention by reading and playing with Poppa's train models to avoid directly contacting grief and guilt
Avoiding deep exploration of self-compassion in sessions with 'changing thoughts is useless'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Believing one 'does not deserve to be lenient with oneself', hard to allow positive experiences in

positive_force: Living with Poppa, able to obtain some emotional support
Deep affection and responsibility toward the pet, willing to reflect and improve
Has proactively sought psychological counseling and expressed willingness to cooperate
Can recall and acknowledge positive moments with the pet (though acceptance is difficult)
negative_force: Intense self-blame and 'should'-style rules maintain the guilt
Excessively personalizing responsibility, difficulty accommodating uncontrollability
Negating positive information, difficulty accepting self-compassion
Worrying about burdening others and reducing help-seeking
Frequent rumination and emotional triggering related to the loss

target_behavior.behavior: Intense guilt and self-reproach (accompanied by repeated rumination)
antecedent: Thinking about the late beloved cat
Seeing old photos or places where the pet used to stay
Interacting with other pets or seeing others walk their pets
target_behavior.core_reason: Blaming the pet's death on oneself, forming a rigid cognition of full responsibility and full control (control fallacy and overgeneralization)
target_behavior.function: Gaining a feeling of 'I can still control/bear it' through self-blame, trying to prevent making mistakes again (self-punishment and atonement)
target_behavior.consequence: Daily life is disrupted, mood remains low, finding it hard to accept support and positive information

target_behavior.behavior: Avoidance/distraction (reading, playing with Poppa's train models) to escape painful emotions
antecedent: When guilt and grief are triggered (photos, familiar places, interacting with other pets)
target_behavior.core_reason: A short-term coping strategy adopted to reduce the intensity of current emotional pain
target_behavior.function: Escaping the unwelcome experiences of guilt and grief, short-term emotional relief
target_behavior.consequence: Short-term relief but not conducive to integrating grief and correcting cognition, the problem persists
